questions.q: What is omnichannel marketing for restaurants?
questions.a: Omnichannel marketing connects all of your restaurant's channels, like your website, app, social media, delivery platforms and dining room, so guests get a consistent experience wherever they meet you. Data from each channel flows into one place. That gives you a complete picture of each guest to personalize your marketing.

questions.q: What is the difference between multichannel and omnichannel marketing?
questions.a: Multichannel marketing runs each channel as a separate entity with its own data. Omnichannel marketing links those channels and gathers their data in one central system. The result is a more consistent guest experience and better information for your decisions.

questions.q: What are the benefits of omnichannel marketing for a restaurant?
questions.a: You give guests the same experience whether they order online or walk in, which builds familiarity and trust. Being present on more apps and platforms helps new guests find you. A central customer database also makes it easier to personalize offers, target ads and plan things like new locations.

questions.q: How do I start an omnichannel marketing strategy for my restaurant?
questions.a: Begin with consistent branding and messaging across every online and in-store channel. Engage with guests wherever they reach out, and make sure online questions get answers as quickly as guests in the dining room. Then unify your customer data, for example with a loyalty program that works for both online and in-store purchases.

questions.q: What are good examples of omnichannel marketing in restaurants?
questions.a: Starbucks offered free Wi-Fi to guests who signed up through its portal, bringing in-store visitors into its digital rewards program. Shake Shack added a mobile app, kiosks, digital pre-ordering, pickup shelves and walk-up windows, all marketed with the same branding. It also offered some limited-time items to app users first to reward loyalty.
